identity.title: Capillary refill time prolonged (>2-3 s, fingertip at heart level, warm room)

technique.how: With the hand at heart level in a warm room, press the distal index finger pad (or nail bed) firmly for 10-15 s until blanched, release, and time return of baseline colour with a watch. Prolonged is >3 s (ICU studies use >2.4-3 s at the fingertip; knee CRT is an alternative site).
technique.prerequisites: Warm extremity and ambient temperature; a second hand or watch to time; consistent pressure (a glass slide can standardise blanching).
technique.contraindications: Not interpretable on a cold, cyanotic or vasoconstricted limb, with peripheral arterial disease, or in the presence of nail polish/false nails.

interpretation.positive_finding: In resuscitated septic shock, a fingertip CRT >2.4 s at 6 h predicts 14-day death with sensitivity 82% and specificity 73%, and marks persisting hypoperfusion. In undifferentiated adults, a prolonged CRT is a weak sign of hypovolemia (sensitivity 26-46%).
interpretation.negative_finding: A normal CRT does not exclude mild-to-moderate hypovolemia in adults (sensitivity 6% after 450 mL loss). In acute circulatory failure, normal CRT only weakly lowers mortality risk (pooled LR- about 0.6).
interpretation.pitfalls: Cold room, cold hands, age and vasoconstriction prolong CRT without hypoperfusion; measurement quality (site, pressure, timing) strongly affects accuracy. CRT is a prognostic/perfusion marker, not a diagnostic test for the cause of shock.
interpretation.changes_what: Prolonged CRT in shock: treat as ongoing hypoperfusion and reassess after resuscitation; normal CRT does not rule out hypovolemia.

estimates.target_condition: Hypovolemia (ED patients with suggestive history and frank hypotension)
estimates.population: 13 adult ED patients with history suggestive of hypovolemia and hypotension; comparison group blood donors
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical hypovolemia group assignment (hypotension); age-sex specific CRT upper limit of normal
estimates.quote: 26% for the orthostatic group, and 46% for the hypotensive group

estimates.target_condition: Hypovolemia (ED patients with suggestive history and abnormal orthostatic vital signs)
estimates.population: 19 adult ED patients with history suggestive of hypovolemia and abnormal orthostatic vital signs
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical hypovolemia group assignment (abnormal orthostatics); age-sex specific CRT upper limit of normal
estimates.quote: 26% for the orthostatic group, and 46% for the hypotensive group

estimates.target_condition: 14-day mortality after initial resuscitation of septic shock (index fingertip CRT >2.4 s at 6 h)
estimates.population: 59 consecutive adults with septic shock, tertiary ICU
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.82/(1-0.73) = 3.0; LR- = (1-0.82)/0.73 = 0.25, from reported sensitivity 82% and specificity 73%
estimates.quote: index CRT at 2.4 s predicted 14-day outcome with a sensitivity of 82% (95% CI [60-95]) and a specificity of 73% (95% CI [56-86])

estimates.target_condition: 14-day mortality after initial resuscitation of septic shock (knee CRT >4.9 s at 6 h)
estimates.population: 59 consecutive adults with septic shock, tertiary ICU
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.82/(1-0.84) = 5.1; LR- = (1-0.82)/0.84 = 0.21, from reported sensitivity 82% and specificity 84%
estimates.quote: knee CRT at 4.9 s predicted 14-day outcome with a sensitivity of 82% (95% CI [60-95]) and a specificity of 84% (95% CI [68-94])

estimates.target_condition: Death in adults with acute circulatory failure (abnormal CRT, study-specific thresholds)
estimates.population: Adults with acute circulatory failure; 13 studies in primary analysis (23 studies, 60,656 patients overall)
estimates.reference_standard: Mortality as reported by each study
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.54/(1-0.72) = 1.9; LR- = (1-0.54)/0.72 = 0.64, from pooled sensitivity 54% and specificity 72%
estimates.quote: pooled sensitivity was 54% (95%CI [43; 64]). The pooled specificity was 72% (95%CI [55; 84])

sources.citation: McGee S, Abernethy WB 3rd, Simel DL. The rational clinical examination. Is this patient hypovolemic? JAMA. 1999;281(11):1022-1029.
Schriger DL, Baraff LJ. Capillary refill--is it a useful predictor of hypovolemic states? Ann Emerg Med. 1991;20(6):601-605.
Ait-Oufella H, Bige N, Boelle PY, et al. Capillary refill time exploration during septic shock. Intensive Care Med. 2014;40(7):958-964.
Jacquet-Lagreze M, Wiart C, Schweizer R, et al. Prognostic value of capillary refill time in adult patients: a systematic review with meta-analysis. Crit Care. 2023;27(1):473.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use CRT to exclude hypovolemia or bleeding in adults; do not interpret on cold, vasoconstricted or peripherally diseased limbs.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Persistently prolonged CRT after initial resuscitation in septic shock marks a high-mortality group and should prompt reassessment of perfusion and escalation, not reassurance.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Inter-rater concordance in ICU was 80% (73-86) for index CRT and 95% (93-98) for knee CRT (Ait-Oufella 2014, abstract); measurement quality strongly affects accuracy.

extraction_notes: Two distinct roles are captured: (a) diagnosis of hypovolemia in ED adults, where the JAMA RCE (source 0) concludes CRT has no proven diagnostic value and the underlying primary study (Schriger 1991, source 1) reports sensitivities 6%/26%/46% but the abstract gives no specificity (specificity is in the paper's tables, not accessible), so those entries carry sensitivity only; (b) prognosis in shock, where Ait-Oufella 2014 (n=59, single centre) and the 2023 Crit Care meta-analysis give sens/spec for mortality. LRs computed from reported sens/spec. The ED hypovolemia groups are tiny (13 and 19 patients). The 2.4 s / 4.9 s thresholds are ICU-derived at 6 h; the title's generic >2-3 s threshold is convention.
